answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on costly, non-refundable identity stakes: each agent bonds real value before it may act, so spinning up a whole garden of fake personas becomes ruinously expensive. Like pigment that permanently stains cloth, a staked reputation cannot be cheaply washed off, and any agent that crosses the ridge into fraud forfeits its bond. That makes one honest identity worth more than a thousand disposable clones.
